question: Can a current-biased Josephson junction take the phase of a microwave current?

provenance.source: Stewart, Appl. Phys. Lett. 12, 277 (1968); McCumber, J. Appl. Phys. 39, 3113 (1968); steps: Shapiro, Phys. Rev. Lett. 11, 80 (1963)

name: overdamped Josephson junction
closure: resistively shunted junction without capacitance; current in units of the critical current, time in units of hbar / (2 e R I_c)
observable: phase of the Josephson oscillation (its frequency is the time-averaged voltage)
